stem: A grouped frequency distribution has these classes: ${=b0} \le x < {=b1}$ with frequency $f$ (unknown); ${=b1} \le x < {=b2}$ with frequency ${=3*k}$; ${=b2} \le x < {=b3}$ with frequency ${=k}$; ${=b3} \le x < {=b4}$ with frequency ${=k}$. Using the class centres, the mean is ${=c}$. Find $f$ and then calculate the standard deviation.
solution: Total frequency ${=8*k}$. Deviations from the mean ${=c}$: $-{=w}$, $0$, ${=w}$, ${=2*w}$.
Variance $={=w*w}$, so the standard deviation is ${=w}$.
notes: Unknown f is solved from the given mean (f=3k). The middle class has frequency 3k and is at the mean, so f is genuinely determined by the other classes. Placeholder parent id.
